headline: tanaike-lab: Human-AI R&D lab publishes urban rain study using Gemini
summary: A new Human-AI virtual R&D system, tanaike-lab, powered by Gemini, successfully executed and published a scientific investigation into urban torrential rain fluid dynamics. It combines human imagination with AI-accelerated logic to overcome traditional researc
details: The tanaike-lab system presents a next-generation R&D paradigm, combining human imagination with AI-accelerated logic. It recently completed a zero-to-one execution of an urban torrential rain fluid dynamics research project, resulting in a fully realized manuscript published on ESS Open Archive.

This system addresses the core bottleneck in modern scientific research: overwhelming operational friction, from numerical solver implementation to manuscript drafting. It also counters the issue of 'AI slop' by ensuring theoretical depth and physical consistency.

tanaike-lab is an advanced, integrated R&D operating system. It unifies Generative AI (LLMs), a 22-Subagent Matrix, Agent Skills, Custom System Hooks, Function Calling, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocols into a dynamic virtual laboratory.

Under the direction of its Principal Investigator and powered by Gemini on the Antigravity CLI, the system executed a complete scientific investigation. The paper, 'Localized Fluid Dynamics Framework for High-Resolution Urban Torrential Rain Prediction,' is now publicly available.

Currently, tanaike-lab is in an active testing phase, continuously evolving through real-world research projects. The long-term goal is to open-source and release the framework to the global research community once its self-evolution reaches full maturity.

A key insight highlights that while the system enforces order and AI accelerates logic, the true human role is to inject novel concepts. tanaike-lab acts as a vanguard where clear human imagination draws new scientific realities out of the dark void.

headline_marked: [[Hackers stole medical records]] from CareCloud, affecting hundreds of thousands
headline: Hackers stole medical records from CareCloud, affecting hundreds of thousands
summary: Healthcare tech giant CareCloud is notifying nearly 350,000 individuals after hackers accessed their medical records, including names, SSNs, and financial data, from an AWS-hosted database.
details: Hundreds of thousands of people are receiving notifications that their medical records were stolen in a cyberattack at U.S. health tech giant CareCloud earlier this year. New disclosures reveal nearly 350,000 individuals have been affected so far, with the number likely to increase.

CareCloud, based in New Jersey, manages patient records for over 45,000 providers across the U.S., including doctors' offices and hospitals. The company handles a vast amount of sensitive medical and billing data for millions of healthcare patients.

According to a data breach notice, hackers gained access to one of CareCloud's electronic health record data stores, hosted on Amazon Web Services, for at least six days between March 10 and March 16. The company confirmed that a hacker "claimed to have exfiltrated data from databases."

The stolen data is extensive, including people's names, postal addresses, Social Security numbers, and government-issued identification numbers like passports and driver's licenses. Financial information, such as bank account details and payment card numbers, alongside a wealth of medical and health-related information, was also compromised.

CareCloud's chief executive has not responded to requests for comment regarding the incident. This breach is part of a series targeting healthcare providers this year, including TriZetto (3.4 million affected) and NYC Health + Hospitals (1.8 million affected).
